question: Does native wrist capture and layer submission stop when lowered and resume when raised in Prey?
claim: Capture remained 1392 while forward HUD capture advanced 1445 to 3281, then resumed on raising the wrist. Capture reached 1495 with zero refusals/faults; 1493 wrist-layer frames. Captured submissions add/remove the wrist quad. Visual placement/readability remains unaccepted.
method: One 3-minute-12-second Prey session, source 27b15fe, candidate DLL identified in run.json, process-scoped xr-sim and xr-tape. Native menu taps loaded existing Talos Lobby save. Fixed head, raised/lowered/raised left grip, then pause and vr.disable. Command replies and exact matching xrEndFrame capture records retained.

identity.reason: Steam binary SHA verified; exact injected candidate SHA and PID recorded.

instrument.reason: Native counters paired with matching xrEndFrame records for four captures; quad coverage placeholder explicitly excluded from proof.

control.reason: Lowered wrist stops capture while forward HUD advances; raising restores capture and third layer. Pause suppresses wrist layer.

scene.reason: Talos Lobby gameplay established in both-eye captures; menu 6 reaches pause.

restore.reason: vr.disable acknowledged, XR torn_down logged, owned PID exited. Temporary settings removed; no preexisting options file, no shared runtime change.

baseline.reason: Panel composition is visibly distorted/misplaced in the simulator. Native capture lifecycle confirmation is not visual acceptance or release approval.

limits: No headset evidence. pixelsCovered=1 is a quad-draw sentinel, not measured area. Simulator matrix convention is a defect candidate, not experimentally isolated here. Trace truncated at 10000 frames, four captures match successful recorded end results. No damage/healing/psi/suit/save-load/performance acceptance.
